$status: Corrected 2026-08-09 against Thupten's reference photographs of real Ü-Tsang chupas. Values in $fromPhotos were read off those garments; everything else is still an unconfirmed guess. Correct anything wrong and move its key into $fromThupten.
$approach: This describes the FINISHED GARMENT SHAPE, not a sewing pattern. The chupa is built directly as a shell around the mannequin — no panels, no seams, no draping solve. Users only ever change colour and material.
$readFromPhotos: The adult skirt is a NEARLY STRAIGHT COLUMN. Measured off Thupten's own drawing and the navy reference garment beside it (2026-08-10), both independently: the hem is about 1.15x the sash, on straight side edges. It is not an A-line. The child's chupa read as 1.8 because children's garments flare; generalising that number to the adult was wrong.

The wrap is the front. Two panels cross: the WEARER'S LEFT panel lies ON TOP, so from the viewer the visible edge is a long diagonal running from the upper right down to the lower left, ending at the side seam at the sash. The wearer's right panel goes underneath, and only its short steep edge from the opposite shoulder down to the point of the V is visible.
Deep V neckline: the two wrap edges cross at about 0.8 of the way from the shoulder to the sash.

Shoulder straps sit INSIDE the shoulder point — the chupa's shoulder is about as wide as its waist, and the honju sleeve emerges outboard of it. Earlier builds pushed the shoulder panel past the shoulder, which read as square slabs.

The chupa carries a DOUBLE STITCH: two rows of topstitching set in from the wrap edge, running its full length and continuing past where the collar stops. Thupten pointed this out 2026-08-10, after it had been mistaken for the neckline running deeper than it does. The V is NOT deep — the fold sags only about 2.5cm below a straight chord from the neck to where it dies out. The stitching is not drawn in the flat — it reads as a hard line at that scale.
THERE IS NO CUFF. The sleeve end is the honju turned back on itself — a fold-up, same cloth. A separate contrast cuff is a modern design idea and this garment does not have one. Thupten 2026-08-10.
The shawl collar is the honju's own neckline folded out over the chupa, so it is always the honju's cloth and colour.

THE TIE IS ALWAYS AT THE BACK. Confirmed by Thupten 2026-08-10. The technical flat shows a bow at the centre front — that pattern was drafted by a non-Tibetan and is wrong on this one point only; everything else in it is correct.

ADULTS. v1 is the adult Ü-Tsang chupa, so the skirt is the slim column of the navy and black reference garments. The flared A-line in the children's chupas is a children's-garment trait and must not drive hemFlare.
The neckline runs CLOSE TO THE NECK. A Tibetan woman's chupa shows no cleavage — the fold crosses high, above the bust, and the neck opening is narrow. Thupten 2026-08-10.

The shoulder seam SLOPES 20-23 degrees off horizontal, neck point high and shoulder point low, and the armhole between the shoulder point and the underarm is CONCAVE — it scoops in, bottoms out, then flares. Standard pattern drafting, confirmed against a pattern piece Thupten supplied 2026-08-10.

The shoulder is NARROW — only a few centimetres of strap between the neck opening and the armhole — and the armhole is correspondingly deep, running OUTWARD from the strap down to the underarm in a long S-curve rather than scooping inward. Thupten's bodice drawing 2026-08-10.
The wrap carries the chupa's own band along its fold edge. NOT doubled — Thupten 2026-08-10.

THE SKIRT WRAPS AT THE CENTRE BACK, not the front. The technical flat shows the overlap running waist to hem down the back on both the chupa and the separate wrap skirt; the front is one clean uninterrupted panel. Since only the front is ever shown, the skirt can stay a closed tube — the opening is on the side nobody sees.
The bodice is FITTED, with waist shaping — it is not a straight tube from shoulder to sash.
The honju's sleeves hang DOWN along the body, close in, tapering to a cuff at the wrist. They do not stand out from the figure.
The honju's collar is a wide shawl collar that folds OUT over the chupa's V, in the honju's own colour. It is the most recognisable feature of the whole outfit and reads at any distance.
A sash in the chupa's own fabric sits at the waist and ties at the back.

The pangden covers the front only, roughly hip width — it does not wrap to the back. It is woven as narrow vertical strips seamed together, each strip carrying its own horizontal stripe program, so the strips do not line up with each other.
The pangden stops short of the hem; the chupa shows below it.
Brocade motifs seen: longevity roundels, floral sprays, endless knots. Phase 5 tintable-brocade material.

$notes.hemFlare: Hem circumference over waist circumference. THE silhouette number. 1.0 is a straight tube; the adult chupa measures 1.15 on two independent reads. Cut, not gathered — the cloth stays smooth.
$notes.wrapEdgeAtCentre: Where the two crossing wrap edges meet, as a fraction of shoulder-to-sash. This is the point of the V.
$notes.waistGatherRatio: Surplus fabric over the shape the skirt is tied to, which gravity pleats. A separate knob from hemFlare: flare is the cut, gather is the surplus. The reference garment is smooth brocade, so this is 1.0.
$notes.vNeckDrop: Shoulder down to where the two wrap edges cross, which is the centre of the collar band, not its lower edge — the collar straddles this line. Measured at about 0.77 of shoulder-to-sash on the navy reference. It has to leave a collar's width of room above the sash, because the over band turns at the crossing and runs horizontally out to the side seam — set it deeper and that run is crushed against the sash.
$notes.backNeckDrop: Shoulder down to the back top edge. Small — the back sits high.
$notes.armholeDrop: Shoulder down to the underarm, where the armhole meets the side seam. An ORDINARY sleeveless armhole — Thupten's technical flat and the orange chupa (2026-08-10) both show a normal curved armhole at about bust height. An earlier build had this at 30, dropping the underarm to the sash, which is not this garment.
$notes.shoulderPanelWidth: Across the shoulder, neck side to arm side. Has to reach the shoulder point: the honju goes UNDER the chupa, so the top of the shoulder is chupa and the sleeve emerges below it. Too narrow and a tab of honju stands above the strap.
$notes.shoulderSlopeDeg: How far the shoulder seam falls from the neck point out to the shoulder point, in degrees off horizontal. Standard women's drafting is 20-23. An angle rather than a drop, so it stays right when the strap width changes. A flat-topped strap is what made the bodice read as a cut-out instead of a garment.
$notes.armholeScoop: How far the armhole curve bites in between the shoulder point and the underarm. It is concave, as drafted — a monotonic sweep between the two gives a wedge, not an armhole.
$notes.shoulderSeamDrop: Floor on how far below the shoulder the honju sleeve may start showing. Normally the emergence point is COMPUTED — the sleeve appears where the arm first gets wider than the chupa covering it — and this is only a guard.
$notes.crossoverWidth: How far the wrap laps past centre front, closing left over right to the wearer's right.
$notes.collarWidth: Width of the honju's shawl collar band where it folds out over the chupa.
$notes.deltoidDrop: How far below the shoulder the sleeve reaches its widest. The deltoid bulges well DOWN the arm, not at the shoulder — a short span reads as a corner rather than a shoulder.
$notes.armholeGap: How far below the shoulder the honju sleeve first appears — it comes OUT OF THE ARMHOLE, just below the chupa's shoulder — not level with the shoulder tip, and not halfway down the arm either. The honju is worn INSIDE the chupa and comes out through the armhole, so a little chupa always shows between the two. Butting them together makes the honju look stuck on the outside.
$notes.wrapEndX: How far from centre the wrap fold dies out. Well inside the side seam — traced off Thupten's line 2026-08-10.
$notes.wrapEndDrop: Shoulder down to where the wrap fold runs out at the far side. It dies out HIGH, around the underbust — Thupten 2026-08-10. Taking it down to the sash drew a long low tail across the ribs that the garment does not have.
$notes.wrapBandWidth: Width of the chupa's OWN band along the wrap edge. The chupa's, not the honju's — it is there whether or not a collar sits over it.
$notes.collarReach: How far along the fold the OVER collar band runs, 0-1. 1 is the fold's whole length.
$notes.collarUnderReach: How far along its fold the UNDER collar band runs, 0-1. It is a FULL band — it runs unbroken from its own shoulder and carries on PAST the crossing so its end is hidden under the other band. Stopping it at the crossing leaves a gap of bare chupa between the two.
$notes.topstitchInset: How far in from the chupa's wrap edge the first row of topstitching sits. Real, but deliberately NOT drawn — at this scale a line competes with the fold. For Phase 5 as a shading detail.
$notes.topstitchGap: Spacing between the two rows of the chupa's double stitch.
$notes.strips: Number of vertical woven strips in the pangden, each with its own stripe program.

pangden.stripeProgram: R3 K1 Y2 G3 K1 W1 B3 M2 K1 O2 T3 K1 R2 Y1 G2 B2 K1 M3 W1 O3
